text:
maya: Quick heads-up: ran a canary across a new model bring-up (raven-v3) for tool-calls with streaming + kv-prefetch batching=ON. Seeing concentrated structured-output parse failures only on the int4 quant variant. Sending raw numbers.
bench-bot: Canary summary: int4 -> 14/200 parse errors, int8 -> 3/200, float16 -> 1/200. Latency/throughput roughly comparable.
alex: Any sample outputs or logs we can inspect? curious whether it's trailing truncation vs hallucinated JSON
maya: Pasting a representative truncated response we captured (stream cut mid-object):
```
{"action": "create_ticket", "params": {"title": "Payment failure", "user_id": "u_12345", "details": "Charge failed at step 3", "attachments": [
  {"type": "screenshot", "url": "https://..."
```
(note: missing closing brackets and trailing quotes)
jun: That looks like a classic streaming boundary cut — but why only int4? Could be tokenization/entropy differences causing earlier EOS or chunking at different byte offsets.
maya: Exactly. Hypothesis: quantized kernels produce slightly different tokenization boundaries under throughput-optimized batching so KV-cache+batching sometimes returns a chunk that ends mid-token more often.
alex: We should avoid heavy-handed fixes that penalize int4 performance for everything. Proposed quick mitigation: append an improbable sentinel at the end of the prompt so final streaming chunk contains a reliable marker; then validate presence of sentinel when assembling stream.
maya: Proposed sentinel approach (suffix-anchor): append a tiny sentinel sequence that the model is extremely unlikely to generate naturally (non-UTF control + UUID). Example we used in canary:
```
--append--\u0007::SENTINEL::b3d9c9a2-9f1e-4b2a-8f45
```
If the assembled stream doesn't contain that suffix, mark response as truncated and invoke json-repair/rescue.
jun: For canary curl test I used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.test/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANARY" \
  -H "X-Canary: true" \
  -d '{"model":"raven-v3-int4","prompt":"<toolcall-prompt>\\n--append--\\u0007::SENTINEL::b3d9c9a2-9f1e-4b2a-8f45","stream":true}'
```
alex: Two questions: 1) false positives if model ever emits that sentinel, 2) repair pipeline complexity. For 1) use a base64/randomized sentinel per-request and check exact bytes; probability of collision is negligible.
liz: Also suggest instrumenting a metric: parse_failure_rate_by_quant_level and parse_success_after_rescue. If parse_success_after_rescue is high, we can keep int4 but route only 10% of production until fixed.
ops-bot: Noted. I'll create an alert template for parse_failure_rate_by_quant_level > 1% sustained over 1m.
bench-bot: Quick re-run with suffix-anchor appended to prompts: int4 errors dropped to 2/200; json-repair succeeded on 11/12 repair attempts (auto-rescue). logs:
```
[2025-09-12T14:02:11Z] canary=1759001111 model=raven-v3-int4 parse_error=true chunk_last_bytes="...\"url\": \"https://...\\n"
[2025-09-12T14:02:11Z] repair_attempt=1 status=jsonfix_applied success=true
[2025-09-12T14:02:11Z] final_parse_success=true
```
maya: That looks promising. Plan proposal:
 1) Push suffix-anchor sentinel canary across 10% of int4 traffic for 24h.
 2) Add automatic repair sequence: (a) attempt jsonfix heuristics (brace completion + ndjson wrap), (b) if repair fails, mirror-call to non-quantized float16 and return that result to caller, (c) emit parse_success_after_rescue telemetry.
 3) Add dashboard + alert for parse_failure_rate_by_quant_level and a per-route breakdown.
alex: I'll open a PR for the canary config + handler (will include per-request randomized sentinel and a length cap so we don't blow token budgets). :thumbsup:
jun: Also add logging: capture last 256 tokens of the stream and the kv-batch-id so we can correlate with the runtime kernel selection and batching window.
bench-bot: I'll schedule automated nightly canaries across int4/int8/float16 with sentinel and collect parse/fix success rates into the eval dashboard. Results posted to https://bench.redwood/canaries/1759001111
liz: Ops note: set default routing to float16 for routes with parse_failure_rate > 2% for 10m then fall back to int8 after manual review.
maya: Cool. I'll create GH issue #4532 with the experiment plan and link the canary PR when alex opens it. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
alex: On it, will tag reviewers from eng-runtime and eng-ml.
ops-bot: Created alert: parse_failure_rate_by_quant_level (threshold=1%).
maya: Closing loop: after 24h canary we'll reconvene and decide whether int4 needs kernel-level patch or longer-term tokenizer adaptation.
